root_cause_criterion.criterion: At `X86_get_insn_id()`, the `find_insn(...)` result must satisfy `i != -1` so the function writes `insn->id` before later X86 naming code reads that public instruction id.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable witness reaches `X86_get_insn_id()` with an internal opcode whose vulnerable `insns[]` table lookup misses, so `i == -1` and the only `insn->id` write is skipped. The fixed program restores the missing mapping entry on the same decode path, making `i != -1` true and causing the public instruction id to be written before the later X86 name lookup.

nodes.description: At the source-level sanitizer sink, `X86_insn_name()` reads the 4-byte `id` argument for `if (id >= X86_INS_ENDING)` while the vulnerable original still has 0 initialized bytes in that scalar.

edges.relation: The initialization state that `X86_get_insn_id()` leaves in `insn->id` is the same state `cs_disasm()` re-reads and re-stores when it executes `insn_cache->id += mci.popcode_adjust`.
The initialization state of the stored public instruction id at `insn_cache->id` is the same state later consumed as the `id` argument in `X86_insn_name()`.
